title: Diagnosing a Failed or Runaway Agentic Session
objective: Deliberately run a longer agentic session on a task open-ended enough that the assistant is likely to drift, then diagnose the drift, roll back the unwanted part with version control, and re-scope a narrower follow-up session that succeeds.
whyThisMatters: Long, less-supervised sessions eventually go off track. Recovering safely without losing the good part of the work is a distinct skill from getting a session right on the first try.
evidence: The original open-ended prompt and a log or transcript summary of what the session actually did
A specific description of where the session drifted from the intended scope (an unrelated file edited, an invented API, or work beyond what was asked)
Git history showing the unwanted portion of the change was isolated and reverted or discarded, while any usable part was kept
The narrower follow-up prompt and evidence that it stayed in scope and passed verification
AI disclosure entry naming the tool/model used, purpose, and what was independently verified
acceptanceCriteria: The drift description names a specific file, decision, or behavior that was outside the original intent, not a general complaint.
Git history shows a revert, reset, or discard operation isolated to the unwanted portion, distinguishable from any kept work.
The follow-up session's diff stays within the boundaries stated in its own narrower prompt.
The follow-up change passes a verification step shown in the evidence.
